trust_decision.summary: Whether a page's content body may be emitted verbatim as HTML is decided at page-initialisation time: hugolib/page__meta.go:initFrontMatter asks the security policy whether the page's already-resolved ContentMediaType is allowed (security.allowContent, text/html denied by default in config/security/securityConfig.go DefaultConfig), while the actual emission is the isHTML branch in hugolib/page__content.go, which skips the content converter and copies the source bytes straight into template.HTML.

landing_point.why: The summary 'XSS via text/html content files' points at the one place where the page's media type decides whether the body is parsed or emitted verbatim: isHTML skips parse/render and the raw bytes are then returned as template.HTML (hugolib/page__content.go:540-544, hugolib/page__content.go:585); an engineer would look here (or at the html->markdown mapping in hugolib/page.go:809-812) first, not in the page-initialisation or security-config layers where the fix actually lands.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: config/security is generic security plumbing with its own policies and tests, and the advisory names content files while the sink is the page content renderer; an engineer can hard-code `if ContentMediaType.IsHTML() { return error }` in initFrontMatter (or escape at the isHTML branch) and leave the config schema, defaults and merge route untouched, which still blocks the reported .html file.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Three legitimate behaviours sit next to the gate. (a) Pages with no content media type at all - synthesized home, section, taxonomy, term, sitemap, robotsTXT and 404 pages carry only a Kind - must not be rejected; the published gate is guarded by !ContentMediaType.IsZero() (fix.diff:141). (b) Content types other than text/html (text/markdown, text/asciidoc, text/x-org, text/rst, text/pandoc and any user-configured type) must stay allowed by default, which requires a deny-only whitelist: Whitelist.Accept returns false for an empty/zero whitelist (acceptNone), and a whitelist of only deny rules implicitly allows everything not denied, so an allow-list of markups or a zero DefaultConfig rejects all content. (c) The html->markdown converter mapping is retained because shortcode inner content rendering still goes through it; an over-broad fix that errors in getContentConverter breaks shortcode inner rendering.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the resource twin of the gated page path: it takes the user-chosen rs.rc.ContentMediaType straight out of the adapter map and builds a resource with it, so a maintainer hardening 'data pulled in by a trusted adapter' would naturally add the policy here too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a CheckAllowedContent call on RenderString's opts.Markup (or on a future html converter registered for .RenderString)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RenderString accepts an arbitrary markup name and returns template.HTML; today 'html' falls through to newContentConverter and errors because no html converter is registered (markup/markup.go:36-98), but a maintainer adding an html renderer would reach the same emission sink and would plausibly gate it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: routing markup.goldmark.renderer.unsafe (raw HTML in Markdown emitted verbatim) through security.allowContent
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the other documented path by which untrusted content bytes reach the output verbatim; a maintainer writing a 'content is untrusted' policy could extend the same check to it rather than leaving it as a separate opt-in.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second consumer of CheckAllowedContent outside page initialisation (e.g. per-output or per-site policy checks)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The existing CheckAllowed* methods are called from several subsystems; placing the content check only in the page assembler leaves the policy helper available for a maintainer to reuse in a wrapper or per-language route.
